# Agent Coaching

`customer_support.support_management.agent_coaching` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**What is the one thing this agent should do differently, and is it actually theirs to fix?**


> Turning what a review found into something an agent can actually do differently on their next ticket. Coaching is a separate discipline from measurement and mostly fails for a structural reason rather than a pedagogical one: the same person usually owns both, so the agent cannot tell whether a conversation is help or evidence, and answers accordingly. The useful unit is a single named behaviour tied to one reviewable interaction — feedback that describes a trend gives nobody anything to hold on Monday morning. Most persistent individual weakness turns out on inspection to be a missing article, an unclear macro or a queue nobody can serve well.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **experimental**


> Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes, playbooks, heuristics, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following quality-assurance in this subdomain. The expertise worth encoding first is the separation from performance_management — coaching that can be cited in a review stops being coaching, and everything else about the capability follows from protecting that boundary. Second is the diagnosis step that almost never happens: before coaching a behaviour, establish whether the agent could have done better with the tools, the knowledge and the queue they had. Coaching an individual for a systems problem is the most common way support teams burn goodwill while their metrics stay flat.
